fault.snapshotTiming: Captured when sub_825EBFB0 faulted while dereferencing the queue item. Its caller sub_825EE3E0 had already stored end-4 at guest address 0x825EE468. The observed end-before-begin difference may therefore be the current consumer's own pop update; it is not proof that the queue was invalid before consumption.
fault.interpretation: The consumer passed a null item into sub_825EBFB0 and faulted reading its reference-count field. Pre-consumption bounds and producer/wait chronology are unknown. Empty-queue consumption, concurrent mutation, stale item, or another guest-state defect remain possible.

focusedTests.scope: Host-session regression coverage only; not a game boot or queue-root-cause test.

observed: Generated guest code in sub_825EED90 invokes sub_825EE3E0 after sub_827AF928; the caller does not branch on the wait helper's return value.
sub_825EE3E0 reads an item at begin, adjusts the queue, then decrements end by four bytes before calling sub_825EBFB0 on the item.

At the later null-item fault inside sub_825EBFB0, the observed end is one slot before begin. Since end has already been decremented in this consumer path, the snapshot cannot establish the pre-pop queue state.

Two generated call-interior entries at 0x82EE2B2C and 0x82EE2B3C encode sc 2 followed by blr in the legacy generated C++ path. Their syscall/import mapping and relevance to this worker remain unproven.
unprovenCandidates: empty-queue consumption due ignored wait result or event/list contract mismatch
concurrent producer/consumer mutation or stale item
generated sc/syscall dispatch or import mapping gap
